name: PA-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Summer Lee holds an overwhelming financial edge, with $1.65 million on hand versus $9,500 for James Hayes
The district's partisan lean favors Democrats by about 10 points
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent
No public polling or expert ratings exist, so the outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: This forecast rests on a Democratic-leaning district, an entrenched incumbent, and a challenger with negligible resources; markets price the Democratic side near 96 percent. With no public polls available, the expected margin stays in the low twenties with relatively wide uncertainty.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Lee, or unexpected polling showing a closer race, would be the main signals of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Summer Lee, the Democratic incumbent, seeks re-election in a Pittsburgh-area district that leans about ten points more Democratic than the country. She was renominated without incident and enters the general election with a large resource edge, having raised roughly $1.5 million and holding $1.6 million on hand. Republican James Hayes has raised about $40,000, with minimal outside spending reported on either side.

No public general-election polling or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district partisanship, incumbency, and the money gap, all of which favor Lee. Prediction markets give the Democratic side roughly a 96 percent chance of winning, consistent with a double-digit expected margin. The race has drawn little attention, and barring unexpected outside investment or a major development, it is expected to remain firmly in the Democratic column.
